newsitem.title: USA: One Democrat drops out of NYC mayoral race.
newsitem.headline: One Democrat drops out of NYC mayoral race.

text.p: Fernando Ferrer, the top elected official in New York City's Bronx borough, Tuesday dropped out of the race to unseat Mayor Rudolph Giuliani.

The moderate Democrat cited a desire to unite the political party against the heavily favoured Giuliani and threw his support behind fellow Democrat Ruth Messinger, who is the borough president of Manhattan.
Aides to Ferrer cited difficulty getting consistent media coverage, organisational problems within the campaign and Giuliani's persistent strong lead in voter opinion polls.
The departure of Ferrer from the race leaves three declared challengers to Giuliani -- Messinger, Brooklyn City Councilman Sal Albanese and activist Rev. Al Sharpton.

"I came to conclude after watching the polls ... that Ruth Messinger and I were tracking each other in the primary, and something had to give here," Ferrer told a news conference on the steps of City Hall. The Bronx borough president said such a primary could be "divisive and potentially destructive."
The primary is scheduled for Sept. 9.
Giuliani's campaign manager Fran Reiter said after Ferrer's announcement that she thinks Messinger, the leading Democratic candidate, is too liberal for most New Yorkers.
"She represents the extreme wing of the Democratic Party," Reiter said. "Ruth espouses ideologies of the past that don't address the problems facing the city."

Giuliani, a former federal prosecutor, was elected to office in 1993 on an anti-crime platform. And polls show voters most pleased with his handling of crime, which has dropped significantly in recent years.
Giuliani is the first Republican to hold the mayor's office in a generation.
Ferrer said he planned to run for a third term as borough president of the Bronx, one of the city's five boroughs. If he had been successful, he would have been the city's first Hispanic mayor.
